cards.title: XNU Linux: Full OS X GUI Userspace on Linux

depth.text: someone got the **macOS desktop** running beside **Linux** by loading macOS's kernel into it

xnulinux builds Apple's open-source **XNU kernel** and runs it inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel; Linux lends it memory, files, networking and GPU access. You need your own macOS installation and a Mac with Xcode to prepare the system disk.

An AI-assisted review argues that a test function concentrated near **prime 2** should produce log 2, but its limit is 0; the article also describes a possible error about bases. **Chapter 13 placeholders** remain where the theorem should be.

glossary.economic rents: Money a business earns beyond what its contribution to creating value would justify.
glossary.product-market fit: When enough customers want a product for it to work as a business.
glossary.ZIRP: Zero Interest Rate Policy: a policy of keeping interest rates at or near zero, which makes borrowing cheaper.
glossary.enshittification: A platform getting worse for users as its owners shift toward extracting more value.
glossary.open world: A game where you can roam around a large map and choose what to do.
glossary.quantization: A way to make a model use less computing power by representing its internal numbers less precisely.
glossary.VRAM: The memory inside a graphics card that holds information the AI needs while running.
glossary.context size: How much of a conversation the AI can keep in mind at once.
glossary.LAN: Local Area Network: devices connected to the same nearby network.
glossary.MoE: Mixture of Experts: a model with many specialist parts that sends each piece of text to only a few of them.
glossary.M3U: A file format for playlists that tells a media player what streams to play.
glossary.XMLTV: A way for apps to share TV schedules, so they can show what's on and when.
glossary.IPTV: Internet Protocol television: TV delivered over the internet to an app or device.
glossary.GTFS-RT: General Transit Feed Specification Realtime: a format for sharing live transit updates, such as bus locations.
glossary.ADS-B: Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast: a way for aircraft to send their positions so receivers on the ground can track them.
glossary.interpolation: Estimating what happened between two known points.
glossary.client-side dead reckoning: Estimating movement on your device from an object's last known position and direction, instead of waiting for another update.
glossary.fixed tick buffer: A small queue of updates that helps show movement at steady time intervals.
glossary.isometric: A way of drawing 3D-looking scenes at an angle, with objects staying the same size rather than shrinking into the distance.
glossary.LLMs: Large language models: computer programs trained on lots of writing that can produce text.
glossary.Lean: A computer program used to write mathematical proofs and check that their steps are correct.
glossary.formalization: Writing mathematics in a precise form that a computer can check.
glossary.dependency graph: A map showing which statements rely on other statements.
glossary.sorry: A placeholder for a missing proof in Lean.
glossary.mathlib: A shared set of math results that Lean proofs can use.
glossary.Riemann hypothesis: A famous math question about the pattern of zeros of a function; this post concerns an attempted proof of it.
glossary.kernel module: A small piece of software that runs inside Linux and adds behavior related to the computer's hardware.
glossary.arm64: A type of processor design; here, the release notes list it as one of OpenBSD's supported systems.
glossary.hypervisor: Software that lets one computer run another operating system in a controlled environment.
glossary.userspace: The part of a computer where ordinary apps run, rather than the operating system's core.
glossary.GPU bridge: The link that lets the macOS side use the Linux host's graphics hardware.
glossary.Riemann Hypothesis: A famous math question about the pattern behind where prime numbers appear.
glossary.generalized Riemann Hypothesis: The same kind of claim extended to a larger family of number-theory functions.
glossary.trace formula: An equality that describes the same thing in two different ways; here, one side is about zeros and the other about primes.
glossary.Hecke L-function: A number-theory function tied to a generalized number system; its zeros are the subject of this proof attempt.
glossary.holomorphic: A function that changes smoothly and predictably throughout the region being discussed.
glossary.Mellin transform: A way to re-express a function so patterns based on multiplication become easier to study.
glossary.Schauder basis: A list of building blocks for expressing objects, where adding the pieces one by one stays controlled.
glossary.Markushevich basis: A way to describe objects using basic pieces, without a guarantee that measuring each piece stays controlled.
glossary.KVM: Kernel-based Virtual Machine: a Linux feature for running virtual machines.
glossary.firmware: The built-in software that tells a device's hardware how to work.
glossary.malware: Software made to harm a computer or get access to it without permission.
glossary.OpenWrt: Software for routers that people can install and change.
glossary.consciousness: The felt, first-person side of experience: what seeing a color or having a thought feels like.
glossary.computational functionalism: The idea that the right kind of calculating, by itself, can produce consciousness.
glossary.substrate independence: The idea that the same computation can run on different materials instead of depending on one particular material.
glossary.autopoiesis: The idea that a living system continually makes and maintains itself.
glossary.anthropomorphism: Describing something nonhuman as if it had human thoughts or feelings.
glossary.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI trained on lots of writing so it can take written questions and produce written answers.
glossary.Turing machine: A simple mathematical model of a computer, used to study what programs can do.
glossary.thread: A group of related messages kept together under one conversation.
glossary.og:description: A short description attached to a webpage that can appear when someone shares its link.
glossary.targeted advertising: Ads chosen using information about who someone is or what they do.
glossary.encryption: A way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
glossary.session replay: A recording that lets a site owner see how someone used a website.
glossary.CIPA: California Invasion of Privacy Act: a California law about recording or intercepting private communications.
glossary.lifestyle diseases: A label for illnesses associated with everyday habits, such as diet or exercise.
glossary.organophosphates: A family of pesticides mentioned in the health estimates.
glossary.WHO: World Health Organization: the UN agency that works on health around the world.
glossary.UNEP: United Nations Environment Programme: the UN body that works on environmental issues.
glossary.IQ: Paired numbers used to represent a radio signal so software can work with it.
glossary.PFAS: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances: a group of “forever chemicals” that persist for a long time in the environment.
glossary.PVC: Polyvinyl chloride: a type of plastic; the comment mentions it in connection with flooring.
glossary.phthalates: A family of chemicals often used to make plastics more flexible.
glossary.NTP: Network Time Protocol: a way for computers to keep their clocks aligned.
glossary.NTP Pool: A shared group of time servers that computers can use to set their clocks.
glossary.Stratum 1 / Stratum 2: Levels in a time-server chain: a Stratum 1 server gets time from a reference source, and a Stratum 2 server gets it from another time server.
glossary.GNSS: Global Navigation Satellite System: satellite signals that help a device work out where it is.
glossary.DDoS: Distributed denial-of-service: an attack that floods a service with traffic so people can't use it.
glossary.FPGA: Field-programmable gate array: a chip that can be set up for different hardware jobs after it is made.
glossary.PTP: Precision Time Protocol: a way for computers on a local network to share very precise time.
glossary.RCE: Remote Code Execution: a flaw that lets an attacker make a computer run their commands from somewhere else.
glossary.AI hacking harness: A setup that lets an AI carry out a series of hacking tasks, often using tools along the way.
glossary.inference: When an AI uses what it learned to answer or act, instead of being trained.
glossary.use-after-free: Trying to use data after it has been discarded.
glossary.-dSAFER: Ghostscript’s option for limiting what a document can do while Ghostscript processes it.
glossary.PostScript: A language used to describe pages and documents, which can also contain instructions for a computer.
glossary.sandbox: A separate, contained space where software can be tested without affecting the rest of a computer or system.
